[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)/// Graph-aware steering footer for a builtin tool result — the content behind
[358](https://docs.rs#358)/// the `with_result_postprocess` hook wired in [`run`]. Only fires against an
[359](https://docs.rs#359)/// active code graph (Function/Class present); everything else returns `None`,
[360](https://docs.rs#360)/// so the framework leaves the result untouched. Cheap: at most two
[361](https://docs.rs#361)/// `has_node_type` read-locks (grep) or a substring test (cypher). The tool has
[362](https://docs.rs#362)/// already released its lock by the time this runs, so there is no re-entrancy.
[363](https://docs.rs#363)fn graph_result_footer(
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    gs: &GraphState,
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    tool: &str,
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    args: &serde_json::Value,
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    body: &str,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)) -> Option<String> {
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    match tool {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)        "grep" => {
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            if !(gs.has_node_type("Function") || gs.has_node_type("Class")) {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                return None;
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            // Zero-match: the framework returns "No matches for pattern '…'."
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            if body.starts_with("No matches for pattern") {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)                return Some(
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                    "No grep matches — but the active code graph indexes the layout, so a \
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                     wrong glob won't hide results there. Try `graph_overview()` then \
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                     `cypher_query`."
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                        .to_string(),
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                );
[382](https://docs.rs#382)            }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)            // Definition-shaped pattern → a structural question grep answers poorly.
[384](https://docs.rs#384)            let p = args
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                .get("pattern")
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                .unwrap_or("")
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                .trim_start_matches(['^', '\\', '('])
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                .trim_start();
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            let definition_shaped = ["fn ", "def ", "class ", "impl ", "func ", "function "]
[391](https://docs.rs#391)                .iter()
[392](https://docs.rs#392)                .any(|kw| p.starts_with(kw));
[393](https://docs.rs#393)            if definition_shaped {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)                Some(
[395](https://docs.rs#395)                    "Tip: that looks like a definition search. The active code graph resolves \
[396](https://docs.rs#396)                     definitions and callers exactly — e.g. `cypher_query(\"MATCH (f:Function \
[397](https://docs.rs#397)                     {title:'NAME'}) RETURN f.file_path, f.line_number\")`, and CALLS edges give \
[398](https://docs.rs#398)                     callers. Reserve grep for literal text (log strings, comments, config keys)."
[399](https://docs.rs#399)                        .to_string(),
[400](https://docs.rs#400)                )
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            } else {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                None
[403](https://docs.rs#403)            }
[404](https://docs.rs#404)        }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)        "cypher_query" if body.contains("qualified_name") => Some(
[406](https://docs.rs#406)            "Tip: `read_code_source(qualified_name=…)` pulls a matched symbol's source body."
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                .to_string(),
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        ),
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        _ => None,
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    }
[411](https://docs.rs#411)}
[412](https://docs.rs#412)
[413](https://docs.rs#413)/// Apply mode-specific bindings — source roots, workspace handle, initial
[414](https://docs.rs#414)/// graph load/build — onto `options`, returning the transformed value.
[415](https://docs.rs#415)fn bind_mode(
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    mode: &Mode,
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    cli: &Cli,
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    graph_state: &GraphState,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    local_active_root: &Arc<RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>>,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    mut options: ServerOptions,
[422](https://docs.rs#422)) -> Result<ServerOptions> {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    match mode {
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        Mode::Graph { path } => {
[425](https://docs.rs#425)            // Exists → load (auto-detect saved mode); absent → create fresh
[426](https://docs.rs#426)            // in --storage mode. Mirrors kglite.open(path, storage=...).
[427](https://docs.rs#427)            let base: PathBuf = if path.exists() {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                let canon = path.canonicalize()?;
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                graph_state.load_kgl(&canon).context("kglite.load failed")?;
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                canon
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            } else {
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                // validate_mode_paths guarantees --storage is set when the
[433](https://docs.rs#433)                // path is missing (else it already bailed with a clean error).
[434](https://docs.rs#434)                let mode_str = cli.storage.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)                    anyhow::anyhow!("--graph path does not exist: {}", path.display())
[436](https://docs.rs#436)                })?;
[437](https://docs.rs#437)                let smode = StorageMode::parse(mode_str).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))?;
[438](https://docs.rs#438)                tracing::info!(
[439](https://docs.rs#439)                    path = %path.display(),
[440](https://docs.rs#440)                    storage = smode.as_str(),
[441](https://docs.rs#441)                    "--graph path does not exist; creating new empty graph"
[442](https://docs.rs#442)                );
[443](https://docs.rs#443)                graph_state
[444](https://docs.rs#444)                    .create_in_mode(path, smode)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)                    .context("kglite create-in-mode failed")?;
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                path.clone()
[447](https://docs.rs#447)            };
[448](https://docs.rs#448)            // P1 (operator feedback): honor the manifest's explicit
[449](https://docs.rs#449)            // `source_root:` / `source_roots:` declaration in `--graph`
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            // mode. The historical behaviour auto-bound the parent of
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            // the `.kgl` file as the source root, which silently
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            // overrode operators who declared a different root in
[453](https://docs.rs#453)            // YAML (e.g. when the .kgl lives in a build dir but the
[454](https://docs.rs#454)            // source files are elsewhere). Now: explicit YAML wins,
[455](https://docs.rs#455)            // auto-bind only when the manifest doesn't declare one.
[456](https://docs.rs#456)            let manifest_roots = manifest
[457](https://docs.rs#457)                .filter(|m| !m.source_roots.is_empty())
[458](https://docs.rs#458)                .map(resolve_source_roots)
[459](https://docs.rs#459)                .transpose()
[460](https://docs.rs#460)                .context("manifest source_root resolution failed")?;
[461](https://docs.rs#461)            let roots = if let Some(rs) = manifest_roots {
[462](https://docs.rs#462)                rs
[463](https://docs.rs#463)            } else if let Some(parent) = base.parent() {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)                vec![parent.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]
[465](https://docs.rs#465)            } else {
[466](https://docs.rs#466)                Vec::new()
[467](https://docs.rs#467)            };
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            if !roots.is_empty() {
[469](https://docs.rs#469)                options = options.with_static_source_roots(roots);
[470](https://docs.rs#470)            }
[471](https://docs.rs#471)        }
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        Mode::SourceRoot { dir } | Mode::Watch { dir } => {
[473](https://docs.rs#473)            let canon = dir.canonicalize()?;
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            options = options.with_static_source_roots(vec![canon.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]);
[475](https://docs.rs#475)            if matches!(mode, Mode::Watch { .. }) {
[476](https://docs.rs#476)                graph_state
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                    .build_code_tree(&canon)
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                    .context("initial code_tree build failed")?;
[479](https://docs.rs#479)            }
[480](https://docs.rs#480)        }
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        Mode::Workspace { dir } => {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)            let canon = dir.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| dir.clone());
[483](https://docs.rs#483)            let gs = graph_state.clone();
[484](https://docs.rs#484)            let hook: workspace::PostActivateHook = Arc::new(move |path, name| {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                tracing::info!(repo = name, "code_tree::build on activate");
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                gs.build_code_tree(path)
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            });
[488](https://docs.rs#488)            // Opening steer: append the graph mini-map to the activation
[489](https://docs.rs#489)            // message (mcp-methods 0.3.46). The post-activate hook above builds
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            // the graph first, so counts are live when this runs. Chained before
[491](https://docs.rs#491)            // the workspace is cloned into `options` (framework caveat).
[492](https://docs.rs#492)            let gs_sum = graph_state.clone();
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            let summary: workspace::ActivationSummaryHook =
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                Arc::new(move |_path, _name| gs_sum.activation_summary());
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            let ws = workspace::Workspace::open(canon, cli.stale_after_days, Some(hook))
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                .context("workspace init failed")?
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                .with_activation_summary(summary);
[498](https://docs.rs#498)            options = options.with_workspace(ws);
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        }
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        Mode::LocalWorkspace { root, .. } => {
[501](https://docs.rs#501)            // mcp-methods `Workspace::open_local(root, hook)` STORES the
[502](https://docs.rs#502)            // post-activate hook but does NOT fire it at open — verified
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            // against mcp-methods 0.3.42 `src/server/workspace.rs`:
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            // `open_local` (`:145`) just stores `post_activate`; the hook
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            // fires only inside `activate()` (`:491-492`), which
[506](https://docs.rs#506)            // `set_root_dir` calls on every swap. So every fire reaching this
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            // closure is a real user activate — build the code-tree on each.
[508](https://docs.rs#508)            //
[509](https://docs.rs#509)            // History (do not re-add): an older mcp-methods contract fired
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            // the hook synchronously inside `open` with the wide
[511](https://docs.rs#511)            // `workspace.root` (~360k files), parsing everything before
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            // returning and blowing past Claude Desktop's 60s `initialize`
[513](https://docs.rs#513)            // window. We added an `initial_activate_seen` deferral to swallow
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            // that one boot fire. mcp-methods has since removed the boot fire
[515](https://docs.rs#515)            // (`open_local` no longer calls the hook), so the deferral was
[516](https://docs.rs#516)            // instead swallowing the user's FIRST `set_root_dir` — leaving the
[517](https://docs.rs#517)            // graph permanently unbuilt in local mode ("No active graph" on
[518](https://docs.rs#518)            // every graph tool). Operator inbox 2026-06-23 (+ original
[519](https://docs.rs#519)            // 2026-06-06 repro). Deferral removed; building eagerly is safe
[520](https://docs.rs#520)            // because mcp-methods no longer fires at boot.
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            //
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            // Active root is captured in a shared RwLock so the watch
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            // callback (later in this fn) can scope its rebuilds.
[524](https://docs.rs#524)            let gs = graph_state.clone();
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            let active_root_for_hook = local_active_root.clone();
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            let hook: workspace::PostActivateHook = Arc::new(move |path, name| {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                if let Ok(mut guard) = active_root_for_hook.write() {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                    *guard = Some(path.to_path_buf());
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                }
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                tracing::info!(repo = name, "code_tree::build on local-workspace activate");
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                // Surface a build failure instead of leaving the tools to
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                // report a bare "No active graph" (operator ask, 2026-06-23).
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                if let Err(e) = gs.build_code_tree(path) {
[534](https://docs.rs#534)                    tracing::error!(
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                        repo = name,
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                        root = %path.display(),
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                        error = %e,
[538](https://docs.rs#538)                        "local-workspace code_tree build failed"
[539](https://docs.rs#539)                    );
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                    return Err(e);
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                }
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                Ok(())
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            });
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            // Opening steer: mini-map on the activation message (see the
[545](https://docs.rs#545)            // github-workspace arm above). Chained before the clone into `options`.
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            let gs_sum = graph_state.clone();
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            let summary: workspace::ActivationSummaryHook =
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                Arc::new(move |_path, _name| gs_sum.activation_summary());
[549](https://docs.rs#549)            let ws = workspace::Workspace::open_local(root.clone(), Some(hook))
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                .context("local-workspace init failed")?
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                .with_activation_summary(summary);
[552](https://docs.rs#552)            options = options.with_workspace(ws);
[553](https://docs.rs#553)        }
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        Mode::Bare => {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)            if let Some(m) = manifest {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                if !m.source_roots.is_empty() {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                    let resolved =
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                        resolve_source_roots(m).context("source root resolution failed")?;
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                    options = options.with_static_source_roots(resolved);
[560](https://docs.rs#560)                }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            }
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    }
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    Ok(options)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)}
[566](https://docs.rs#566)
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// Client-side tool-discovery steer, folded into workspace-mode
[568](https://docs.rs#568)/// `instructions` so every `--workspace` / `workspace.kind: local`
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// deployment emits it on `initialize` without copy-pasting it into each
[570](https://docs.rs#570)/// manifest. It complements the 0.12.6 in-band steering (graph-over-grep
[571](https://docs.rs#571)/// vocabulary in tool descriptions, the activation mini-map, the result
[572](https://docs.rs#572)/// footer) by making the *"search the registry"* instruction explicit for
[573](https://docs.rs#573)/// lazy-tool-discovery clients (Codex / code_mode / tool-search), which can
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// surface only `grep`/`read_source` on a broad first query and miss the
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// always-registered graph tools. Skipped when the manifest already carries
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// equivalent guidance (see the dedup check in `run_async`).
[577](https://docs.rs#577)const DISCOVERY_STEER: &str = "Tool discovery: graph_overview and cypher_query are ALWAYS registered. \
[578](https://docs.rs#578)If a broad first tool-search surfaces only grep/read_source, search your tool registry for 'cypher' or \
[579](https://docs.rs#579)'graph_overview' and load those before falling back to grep — a discovery miss does not mean the graph \
[580](https://docs.rs#580)path is unavailable.";
[581](https://docs.rs#581)
[582](https://docs.rs#582)/// Fold [`DISCOVERY_STEER`] into `options.instructions` for the two
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// workspace modes. Appends (preserving any manifest `instructions:`) or
[584](https://docs.rs#584)/// sets it when none exists; bails when the text already mentions the
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// always-registered graph tools so an opted-in manifest isn't duplicated.
[586](https://docs.rs#586)fn apply_discovery_steer(mode: &Mode, mut options: ServerOptions) -> ServerOptions {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    if !matches!(mode, Mode::Workspace { .. } | Mode::LocalWorkspace { .. }) {
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        return options;
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    }
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    let already = options
[591](https://docs.rs#591)        .instructions
[592](https://docs.rs#592)        .as_deref()
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        .is_some_and(|s| s.to_lowercase().contains("always registered"));
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    if already {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        return options;
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    }
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    options.instructions = Some(match options.instructions.take() {
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        Some(existing) if !existing.trim().is_empty() => format!("{existing}\n\n{DISCOVERY_STEER}"),
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        _ => DISCOVERY_STEER.to_string(),
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    });
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    options
[602](https://docs.rs#602)}
[603](https://docs.rs#603)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)async fn run_async(cli: Cli, py_embedder_factory: Option<PyEmbedderFactory>) -> Result<()> {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    init_tracing();
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    let mode = pick_mode(&cli);
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    validate_mode_paths(&mode, &cli)?;
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    let manifest = load_manifest(&cli, &mode).context("manifest load failed")?;
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    // Manifest `workspace.kind: local` wins over CLI flags — promote before
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    // mode-specific binding so the rest of boot sees `Mode::LocalWorkspace`.
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    let mode = promote_local_workspace(mode, manifest.as_ref())?;
[614](https://docs.rs#614)
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    // Load `.env` before anything reads env vars (notably the GitHub
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    // tools' `GITHUB_TOKEN` auth check). Walk-up start point matches
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    // the framework binary's choice in `mcp-server`'s own main: the
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    // mode's directory for source-aware modes, cwd for bare. Explicit
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    // `env_file:` in the manifest overrides walk-up. Returns the path
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    // actually loaded so the boot summary can name it.
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    let env_start_dir = resolve_env_start_dir(&mode);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    let env_file_loaded = load_env_for_mode(manifest.as_ref(), &env_start_dir)
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        .context("manifest env_file load failed")?;
[624](https://docs.rs#624)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    let mut options = ServerOptions::from_manifest(manifest.as_ref(), fallback_name(&mode));
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    if cli.name.is_some() {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        options.name = cli.name.clone();
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    // Fold the lazy-tool-discovery steer into workspace-mode instructions so
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    // code-mode / tool-search clients get the "search the registry for cypher"
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    // guidance by default, without every deployment copy-pasting it.
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    let options = apply_discovery_steer(&mode, options);
[633](https://docs.rs#633)
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    // The github-workspace (open-source) mode ingests each cloned repo's
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    // markdown as `:Doc` nodes and links them to code (MENTIONS/DOCUMENTS) —
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    // a repo's prose is part of its intelligence. Local / file / graph modes
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    // keep the lean code-only graph.
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    let include_docs = matches!(mode, Mode::Workspace { .. });
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    // extensions.value_codecs: build the manifest-declared, position-scoped
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    // literal codecs (prefix / map / regex). Passed to the engine via
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    // ExecuteOptions per query — decode on the way in, encode on the way out.
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    // Empty when absent; a malformed block errors at boot, not per-query.
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    let value_codecs = match manifest.as_ref() {
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        Some(m) => value_codecs::from_manifest(m.extensions.get("value_codecs"))
[645](https://docs.rs#645)            .context("extensions.value_codecs parse failed")?,
[646](https://docs.rs#646)        None => Vec::new(),
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    };
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    let value_codecs = if value_codecs.is_empty() {
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        None
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    } else {
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        Some(Arc::new(value_codecs))
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    };
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    let graph_state = GraphState::new(include_docs).with_value_codecs(value_codecs);
[654](https://docs.rs#654)
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    // Shared "active root" slot for local-workspace mode. Populated
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    // by the post-activate hook on each `set_root_dir`; read by the
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    // watch callback to scope rebuilds. Stays `None` until the first
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    // `set_root_dir` (the boot-time activate is intentionally
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    // deferred — see `Mode::LocalWorkspace` arm below for why).
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    // Other modes never write to it.
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    let local_active_root: Arc<RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>> = Arc::new(RwLock::new(None));
[662](https://docs.rs#662)
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    // Mode-specific bindings: source roots, workspace handle, initial graph
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    // build. Extracted to `bind_mode` so this boot fn reads as a sequence of
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    // named phases.
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    let options = bind_mode(
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        &mode,
[668](https://docs.rs#668)        &cli,
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        manifest.as_ref(),
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        &graph_state,
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        &local_active_root,
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        options,
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    )?;
[674](https://docs.rs#674)
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    // Runtime graph-over-grep steering (mcp-methods 0.3.46 result-postprocess
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    // hook): append a one-line footer to a builtin tool result at the moment of
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    // a likely misuse — a definition-shaped or zero-match `grep`, or a
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    // `cypher_query` result carrying `qualified_name`. Delivered on the RESULT
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    // (read every call), it corrects course where the load-once tool
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    // description could not (petekSuite field report 2026-07-02). Returns `None`
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    // — leaving the result byte-for-byte unchanged — unless a code graph is
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    // active and the shape matches, so non-code deployments are untouched.
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    let options = {
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        let gs = graph_state.clone();
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        options.with_result_postprocess(Arc::new(
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            move |tool: &str, args: &serde_json::Value, body: &str, _ctx: &ResultCtx| {
[687](https://docs.rs#687)                graph_result_footer(&gs, tool, args, body)
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            },
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        ))
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    };
[691](https://docs.rs#691)
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    // Snapshot the dynamic source-roots provider before we move
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    // `options` into the McpServer. The `read_code_source` tool
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    // queries it on every call so workspace-mode active-repo swaps
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    // immediately re-target file resolution.
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    let source_roots_provider = options.source_roots.clone();
[697](https://docs.rs#697)
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    // P4 + P5 (operator feedback): builtin toggles from the manifest.
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    //   - P5 `save_graph`: gate registration on
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    //     `builtins.save_graph: true`. Historically always-on,
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    //     exposing a destructive operation to the agent on every
[702](https://docs.rs#702)    //     graph regardless of intent.
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    //   - P4 `temp_cleanup: on_overview`: wipe `temp/` on every bare
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    //     `graph_overview()`. Historically parsed-but-ignored.
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    // Manifest base dir — used by both csv_http_server (to resolve
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    // `dir:` against the YAML location) and temp_cleanup (to find the
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    // directory to wipe). Falls back to cwd when there's no manifest.
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    let manifest_base: PathBuf = manifest
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        .as_ref()
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        .and_then(|m| m.yaml_path.parent().map(|p| p.to_path_buf()))
[711](https://docs.rs#711)        .unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(".")));
[712](https://docs.rs#712)
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    // `extensions.csv_http_server:` opt-in CSV-over-HTTP listener.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    // When configured we spawn a tokio task to serve files out of
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    // the directory; the `cypher_query` tool sees the same config
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    // and writes `FORMAT CSV` results to that directory, returning
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    // a URL instead of an inline CSV blob.
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    let csv_http_cfg = match manifest.as_ref() {
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        Some(m) => match m.extensions.get("csv_http_server") {
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            Some(raw) => csv_http::CsvHttpConfig::from_manifest_value(raw, &manifest_base)
[721](https://docs.rs#721)                .context("extensions.csv_http_server parse failed")?,
[722](https://docs.rs#722)            None => None,
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        },
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        None => None,
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    };
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    if let Some(cfg) = csv_http_cfg.as_ref() {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        csv_http::spawn(cfg.clone())
[728](https://docs.rs#728)            .await
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            .context("csv_http_server failed to bind")?;
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    }
[731](https://docs.rs#731)
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    let builtins = tools::Builtins {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        save_graph: manifest
[734](https://docs.rs#734)            .as_ref()
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            .map(|m| m.builtins.save_graph)
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            .unwrap_or(false)
[737](https://docs.rs#737)            // Write mode implies save_graph (an agent that mutates needs to
[738](https://docs.rs#738)            // persist) so `--writable` alone gives the full workbench.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            || cli.writable,
[740](https://docs.rs#740)        writable: cli.writable,
[741](https://docs.rs#741)        temp_cleanup_on_overview: manifest
[742](https://docs.rs#742)            .as_ref()
[743](https://docs.rs#743)            .map(|m| {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                matches!(
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                    m.builtins.temp_cleanup,
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                    mcp_methods::server::manifest::TempCleanup::OnOverview
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                )
[748](https://docs.rs#748)            })
[749](https://docs.rs#749)            .unwrap_or(false),
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        // 0.9.19 fix: temp_cleanup target dir was hardcoded to `./temp`
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        // (cwd-relative) — that's the wrong place to look when the
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        // server's cwd doesn't match the manifest's parent. Resolve
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        // against the manifest base, reusing the csv_http_server
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        // directory when configured so both sides of the CSV pipeline
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        // agree on what counts as "the temp dir".
[756](https://docs.rs#756)        temp_dir: Some(
[757](https://docs.rs#757)            csv_http_cfg
[758](https://docs.rs#758)                .as_ref()
[759](https://docs.rs#759)                .map(|c| c.dir.clone())
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                .unwrap_or_else(|| manifest_base.join("temp")),
[761](https://docs.rs#761)        ),
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    };
[763](https://docs.rs#763)
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    let csv_http_arc = csv_http_cfg.map(Arc::new);
[765](https://docs.rs#765)
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    let mut server = McpServer::new(options);
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    tools::register(
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        &mut server,
[769](https://docs.rs#769)        graph_state.clone(),
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        builtins,
[771](https://docs.rs#771)        csv_http_arc.clone(),
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    );
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    code_source::register(
[774](https://docs.rs#774)        &mut server,
[775](https://docs.rs#775)        graph_state.clone(),
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        source_roots_provider.clone(),
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    )
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    .context("read_code_source registration failed")?;
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    explore::register(
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        &mut server,
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        graph_state.clone(),
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        source_roots_provider.clone(),
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    )
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    .context("explore registration failed")?;
[785](https://docs.rs#785)
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    // `extensions.embedder:` in the manifest selects the embedding
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    // backend for `text_score()`:
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    //   - `backend: fastembed` — the Rust-native fastembed-rs adapter
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    //     (cargo `--features fastembed`). The only option for the
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    //     standalone libpython-free binary.
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    //   - `backend: python` — a fastembed-py model, built by the wheel's
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    //     `_run_mcp_server` factory and wrapped in a `PyEmbedderAdapter`.
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    //     Only available when a factory is supplied (the pip-hosted
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    //     server); the cargo binary rejects it with a clear message.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    if let Some(m) = manifest.as_ref() {
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        if let Some(embedder) = build_embedder_from_manifest(m, py_embedder_factory.as_ref())? {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)            graph_state
[798](https://docs.rs#798)                .bind_embedder(embedder)
[799](https://docs.rs#799)                .context("graph.set_embedder_native failed")?;
[800](https://docs.rs#800)        }
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    }
[802](https://docs.rs#802)
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    // YAML-declared `tools[].cypher` entries. The mcp-methods framework
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    // parses them into `manifest.tools` but stays domain-agnostic and
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    // doesn't know how to run Cypher — so the kglite shim owns the
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    // registration loop, using the framework's now-public
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    // `build_tool_attr` plus an in-shim runner that dispatches into the
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    // active graph's `cypher(template, params=args)` method.
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    if let Some(m) = manifest.as_ref() {
[810](https://docs.rs#810)        let runner = cypher_tools::make_runner(graph_state.clone(), csv_http_arc.clone());
[811](https://docs.rs#811)        let registered = cypher_tools::register_cypher_tools(&mut server, m, runner)
[812](https://docs.rs#812)            .context("YAML cypher tool registration failed")?;
[813](https://docs.rs#813)        if registered > 0 {
[814](https://docs.rs#814)            tracing::info!(count = registered, "manifest cypher tools registered");
[815](https://docs.rs#815)        }
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    }
[817](https://docs.rs#817)
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    // Watch handler: rebuild on every debounced change batch. Both
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    // explicit `--watch DIR` and `manifest.workspace.kind: local` with
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    // `watch: true` wire the same change-handler shape.
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    let watch_handle = match &mode {
[822](https://docs.rs#822)        Mode::Watch { dir } => {
[823](https://docs.rs#823)            let canon = dir.canonicalize()?;
[824](https://docs.rs#824)            let gs = graph_state.clone();
[825](https://docs.rs#825)            let cb: watch::ChangeHandler = Arc::new(move |paths| {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)                // Skip when no changed path is a file code_tree parses
[827](https://docs.rs#827)                // — a `cargo build` / `npm install` storm of `.rlib` /
[828](https://docs.rs#828)                // `node_modules/` events would otherwise needlessly
[829](https://docs.rs#829)                // tag a rebuild. Cheap predicate (just an ext lookup).
[830](https://docs.rs#830)                let any_code = paths
[831](https://docs.rs#831)                    .iter()
[832](https://docs.rs#832)                    .any(|p| is_graph_relevant(p, gs.include_docs()));
[833](https://docs.rs#833)                if !any_code {
[834](https://docs.rs#834)                    return;
[835](https://docs.rs#835)                }
[836](https://docs.rs#836)                // Tag for rebuild — the actual work happens on the
[837](https://docs.rs#837)                // next MCP tool call via ensure_code_tree_fresh.
[838](https://docs.rs#838)                // Cheap: no rebuild on the watcher thread, ms-scale.
[839](https://docs.rs#839)                gs.tag_code_tree_dirty(canon.clone());
[840](https://docs.rs#840)            });
[841](https://docs.rs#841)            maybe_watch(Some(dir), Some(cb))?
[842](https://docs.rs#842)        }
[843](https://docs.rs#843)        Mode::LocalWorkspace { root, watch: true } => {
[844](https://docs.rs#844)            // Hand mcp-methods the wide `workspace.root` to monitor —
[845](https://docs.rs#845)            // FSEvents/inotify only emit events for files inside the
[846](https://docs.rs#846)            // subtree, so watching wide is cheap. Filtering happens
[847](https://docs.rs#847)            // in the callback.
[848](https://docs.rs#848)            //
[849](https://docs.rs#849)            // Operator inbox 2026-05-25: pre-fix this captured
[850](https://docs.rs#850)            // `workspace.root` and rebuilt the entire wide tree on
[851](https://docs.rs#851)            // every event (build storm on any `cargo build` /
[852](https://docs.rs#852)            // editor save anywhere in the sandbox). Fix: read the
[853](https://docs.rs#853)            // shared `local_active_root` (populated by the
[854](https://docs.rs#854)            // post-activate hook above on each `set_root_dir`),
[855](https://docs.rs#855)            // skip when nothing changed under the active root,
[856](https://docs.rs#856)            // rebuild against the active root only.
[857](https://docs.rs#857)            let gs = graph_state.clone();
[858](https://docs.rs#858)            let active_root_for_watch = local_active_root.clone();
[859](https://docs.rs#859)            let cb: watch::ChangeHandler = Arc::new(move |paths| {
[860](https://docs.rs#860)                let active = match active_root_for_watch.read() {
[861](https://docs.rs#861)                    Ok(g) => g.clone(),
[862](https://docs.rs#862)                    Err(_) => return,
[863](https://docs.rs#863)                };
[864](https://docs.rs#864)                let Some(active) = active else {
[865](https://docs.rs#865)                    // No `set_root_dir` yet; nothing to rebuild.
[866](https://docs.rs#866)                    return;
[867](https://docs.rs#867)                };
[868](https://docs.rs#868)                // Two-stage filter: (1) inside the active root,
[869](https://docs.rs#869)                // (2) is a code file `code_tree` would parse. The
[870](https://docs.rs#870)                // second filter skips `cargo build` /
[871](https://docs.rs#871)                // `node_modules/` storms that otherwise tag a
[872](https://docs.rs#872)                // rebuild for changes the parser doesn't see.
[873](https://docs.rs#873)                let any_under_active_and_code = paths
[874](https://docs.rs#874)                    .iter()
[875](https://docs.rs#875)                    .any(|p| p.starts_with(&active) && is_graph_relevant(p, gs.include_docs()));
[876](https://docs.rs#876)                if !any_under_active_and_code {
[877](https://docs.rs#877)                    return;
[878](https://docs.rs#878)                }
[879](https://docs.rs#879)                // Tag for rebuild; the actual rebuild fires on the
[880](https://docs.rs#880)                // next MCP tool call (ensure_code_tree_fresh).
[881](https://docs.rs#881)                gs.tag_code_tree_dirty(active.clone());
[882](https://docs.rs#882)            });
[883](https://docs.rs#883)            maybe_watch(Some(root), Some(cb))?
[884](https://docs.rs#884)        }
[885](https://docs.rs#885)        _ => None,
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    };
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    let _watch_handle = watch_handle;
[888](https://docs.rs#888)

[974](https://docs.rs#974)/// Evaluates `applies_when:` predicates that depend on kglite's
[975](https://docs.rs#975)/// runtime graph state. The framework dispatches `tool_registered:`
[976](https://docs.rs#976)/// and `extension_enabled:` itself; this evaluator only handles the
[977](https://docs.rs#977)/// two domain predicates that require knowing what node types and
[978](https://docs.rs#978)/// properties the active graph carries.
[979](https://docs.rs#979)///
[980](https://docs.rs#980)/// Returning `None` for an unrecognised clause marks the predicate
[981](https://docs.rs#981)/// `Unknown` upstream — the framework's safe default suppresses the
[982](https://docs.rs#982)/// skill when any clause is `Unknown`, which prevents a typo'd
[983](https://docs.rs#983)/// predicate from silently activating a skill against the wrong
[984](https://docs.rs#984)/// domain.
[985](https://docs.rs#985)struct KglitePredicateEvaluator {
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    state: GraphState,
[987](https://docs.rs#987)}
[988](https://docs.rs#988)
[989](https://docs.rs#989)impl SkillPredicateEvaluator for KglitePredicateEvaluator {
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    fn evaluate(&self, clause: &PredicateClause<'_>) -> Option<bool> {
[991](https://docs.rs#991)        match clause {
[992](https://docs.rs#992)            PredicateClause::GraphHasNodeType(types) => {
[993](https://docs.rs#993)                Some(types.iter().any(|t| self.state.has_node_type(t)))
[994](https://docs.rs#994)            }
[995](https://docs.rs#995)            PredicateClause::GraphHasProperty {
[996](https://docs.rs#996)                node_type,
[997](https://docs.rs#997)                prop_name,
[998](https://docs.rs#998)            } => Some(self.state.has_property(node_type, prop_name)),
[999](https://docs.rs#999)            // Framework-internal predicates — `tool_registered` and
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)            // `extension_enabled` are dispatched against ServerOptions
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            // by the framework itself, not via this evaluator.
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            _ => None,
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        }
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    }
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)}
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)/// Read `manifest.extensions.embedder.{library, model, …}` and build the
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)/// corresponding [`kglite::api::Embedder`]. Returns `Ok(None)` when no
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)/// `embedder:` is declared, `Err` on validation failures.
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)///
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)/// The `library` field names the embedding engine; the host (Rust vs Python)
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)/// is inferred from it:
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)/// - `fastembed-rs` — the Rust-native fastembed-rs adapter (cargo
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)///   `--features fastembed`; the only option on the standalone binary).
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)/// - any other value, or a `factory:` escape — a Python embedding library
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)///   (`fastembed`, `sentence-transformers`, …) built by `py_embedder_factory`
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)///   (supplied only by the pip-hosted server). The whole config object is
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)///   handed to Python as JSON, so the library set + its options live entirely
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)///   on the Python side (`kglite._mcp_embed`) — adding a library never touches
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)///   this function.
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)fn build_embedder_from_manifest(
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)    manifest: &Manifest,
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)    py_embedder_factory: Option<&PyEmbedderFactory>,
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn kglite::api::Embedder>>> {
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)    let Some(raw) = manifest.extensions.get("embedder") else {
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        return Ok(None);
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)    };
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)    let obj = raw
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        .as_object()
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("extensions.embedder must be a mapping (got: {raw:?})"))?;
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)    // `fastembed-rs` is the only Rust-hosted engine; everything else (and any
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)    // `factory:`) is a Python library hosted by the wheel. Default to a Python
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)    // library so the common pip case needs only `library: + model:`.
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)    let library = obj.get("library").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)    let is_rust = library == Some("fastembed-rs");
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)    if is_rust {
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)        let model = obj.get("model").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).ok_or_else(|| {
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)            anyhow::anyhow!("extensions.embedder.model is required for library: fastembed-rs")
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)        })?;
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)        return build_rust_embedder(model);
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)    }
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)    // Python-hosted: hand the whole config object to the Python factory, which
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)    // picks the library, builds the model, and wraps it. The cargo binary
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)    // supplies no factory.
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)    let factory = py_embedder_factory.ok_or_else(|| {
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)        let lib = library.unwrap_or("<a Python library>");
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)        anyhow::anyhow!(
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)            "extensions.embedder.library = {lib:?} is a Python embedding library, but the \
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)             standalone `cargo install kglite-mcp-server` binary has no Python interpreter to \
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)             host it. Either run the server from the kglite wheel (`pip install kglite`, then \
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)             `pip install {lib}`), or use `library: fastembed-rs` with `cargo install \
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)             kglite-mcp-server --features fastembed`."
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)        )
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    })?;
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    let config_json = serde_json::to_string(raw)
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("serializing extensions.embedder failed: {e}"))?;
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    let embedder = factory(&config_json)
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("python embedder construction failed: {e}"))?;
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    tracing::info!(library = ?library, "registered python embedder");
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)    Ok(Some(embedder))
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)}
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)/// Build the Rust-native fastembed-rs embedder (`library: fastembed-rs`).
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)/// Gated on the `fastembed` cargo feature; the default build errors with a
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)/// rebuild hint (the feature is off by default because ort-sys has a flaky
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)/// upstream binary download).
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)#[cfg(feature = "fastembed")]
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)fn build_rust_embedder(model: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn kglite::api::Embedder>>> {
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)    let adapter = kglite::api::FastEmbedAdapter::new(model)
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("fastembed-rs init failed: {e}"))?;
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)    tracing::info!(model, "registered Rust-native (fastembed-rs) embedder");
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)    Ok(Some(Arc::new(adapter)))
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)}
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)#[cfg(not(feature = "fastembed"))]
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)fn build_rust_embedder(_model: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<dyn kglite::api::Embedder>>> {
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)    anyhow::bail!(
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)        "extensions.embedder.library = \"fastembed-rs\" requires this binary to be built with \
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)         the `fastembed` feature: `cargo install kglite-mcp-server --features fastembed`. The \
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)         default build excludes it because its ort-sys dependency has a flaky upstream binary \
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)         download. (If you are running the pip wheel, use a Python library instead — e.g. \
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)         `library: sentence-transformers` with `pip install sentence-transformers`.)"
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)    )
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)}
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)fn print_boot_summary(
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)    mode: &Mode,
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)    manifest: Option<&Manifest>,
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    graph_state: &GraphState,
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)    env_file_loaded: Option<&std::path::Path>,
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)) {
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)    let label = match mode {
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)        Mode::Graph { path } => format!("graph [{}]", path.display()),
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)        Mode::SourceRoot { dir } => format!("source-root [{}]", dir.display()),
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        Mode::Workspace { dir } => format!("workspace [{}]", dir.display()),
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        Mode::LocalWorkspace { root, watch } => format!(
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)            "local-workspace [{}{}]",
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)            root.display(),
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            if *watch { " +watch" } else { "" }
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)        ),
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)        Mode::Watch { dir } => format!("watch [{}]", dir.display()),
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)        Mode::Bare => "bare".to_string(),
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)    };
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)    let mut parts = vec![format!("mode: {label}")];
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)    if let Some(p) = env_file_loaded {
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        parts.push(format!("env: {}", p.display()));
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)    } else {
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)        parts.push("env: (no .env found)".to_string());
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)    }
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)    if let Some(m) = manifest {
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)        parts.push(format!("manifest: {}", m.yaml_path.display()));
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)    }
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)    if let Some((nodes, edges)) = graph_state.schema() {
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)        parts.push(format!("graph: {nodes} nodes, {edges} edges"));
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)    }
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)    eprintln!("kglite-mcp-server: {}", parts.join("; "));
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)}

[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)mod discovery_steer_tests {

[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)    use std::path::PathBuf;

# run in kglite_mcp_server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kglite-mcp-server/0.12.9/kglite_mcp_server/fn.run.html

## Expand description

Run the MCP server to completion over stdio.

`args` is a full argv vector (program name in `args[0]`, as clap
expects). The binary passes `std::env::args()`; the PyO3 wrapper
passes a synthesised `["kglite-mcp-server", ...sys.argv[1:]]`.

Synchronous by design (see CLAUDE.md “core is sync, bindings own
async”): this builds its own multi-thread tokio runtime and blocks
on the stdio serve loop. The PyO3 wrapper calls it inside
`py.detach(...)`, so the GIL is released for the server’s entire
lifetime and the Python process simply *becomes* the server.

---

# run_with_embedder_factory in kglite_mcp_server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kglite-mcp-server/0.12.9/kglite_mcp_server/fn.run_with_embedder_factory.html

Like run, but with an optional Python-embedder factory for the
extensions.embedder.library Python path (sentence-transformers /
fastembed). The standalone binary calls run (no factory); the
kglite wheel passes a factory that builds the named Python embedder.

# PyEmbedderFactory in kglite_mcp_server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kglite-mcp-server/0.12.9/kglite_mcp_server/type.PyEmbedderFactory.html

## Expand description

Builds a graph embedder from the manifest’s `extensions.embedder` config
(passed as a JSON string), on demand.

This is the seam that lets the **pip-hosted** server use *any* Python
embedding library (`extensions.embedder.library: sentence-transformers`,
`fastembed`, or a `factory:` escape) without the libpython-free library
knowing anything about Python: the kglite-py wrapper hands the config JSON
to a Python factory (`kglite._mcp_embed`) which picks the library, builds
the model, and wraps it in a `PyEmbedderAdapter` (GIL re-acquired only for
the embed call). The standalone cargo binary passes no factory, so a Python
library errors there with a clear message; it uses `library: fastembed-rs`
(the Rust `FastEmbedAdapter`) instead.

The argument is the whole `extensions.embedder` JSON object, so new fields
(library / model / factory / kwargs / …) flow through to Python without any
Rust change. `Send` because `run_with_embedder_factory` may move it into the
tokio runtime’s future.

## Aliased Type[§](https://docs.rs#aliased-type)

`pub struct PyEmbedderFactory(/* private fields */);`

# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1.0.102/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

# indexmap - Rust

## Expand description

[ IndexMap](https://docs.rs/map/struct.IndexMap.html) is a hash table where the iteration order of the key-value
pairs is independent of the hash values of the keys.

[ IndexSet](https://docs.rs/set/struct.IndexSet.html) is a corresponding hash set using the same implementation and
with similar properties.

and `HashSet`, but they also have some features of note:- The ordering semantics (see their documentation for details)

use fnv::FnvBuildHasher;

type FnvIndexMap<K, V> = IndexMap<K, V, FnvBuildHasher>;

let std: IndexSet<i32> = (0..100).collect();

```

# log - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/log/^0.4.29/

## Expand description

A lightweight logging facade.

The `log` crate provides a single logging API that abstracts over the
actual logging implementation. Libraries can use the logging API provided
by this crate, and the consumer of those libraries can choose the logging
implementation that is most suitable for its use case.

If no logging implementation is selected, the facade falls back to a “noop” implementation that ignores all log messages. The overhead in this case is very small - just an integer load, comparison and jump.

A log request consists of a *target*, a *level*, and a *body*. A target is a
string which defaults to the module path of the location of the log request,
though that default may be overridden. Logger implementations typically use
the target to filter requests based on some user configuration.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The basic use of the log crate is through the five logging macros: [ error!](https://docs.rs/macro.error.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/macro.warn.html)

`warn!`[,](https://docs.rs/macro.info.html)

`info!`[and](https://docs.rs/macro.debug.html)

`debug!`[where](https://docs.rs/macro.trace.html)

`trace!``error!` represents the highest-priority log messages
and `trace!` the lowest. The log messages are filtered by configuring
the log level to exclude messages with a lower priority.
Each of these macros accept format strings similarly to [.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/macro.println.html)

`println!`Avoid writing expressions with side-effects in log statements. They may not be evaluated.

[§](https://docs.rs#in-libraries)In libraries

Libraries should link only to the `log` crate, and use the provided
macros to log whatever information will be useful to downstream consumers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use log::{info, warn};
pub fn shave_the_yak(yak: &mut Yak) {
    info!(target: "yak_events", "Commencing yak shaving for {yak:?}");
    loop {
        match find_a_razor() {
            Ok(razor) => {
                info!("Razor located: {razor}");
                yak.shave(razor);
                break;
            }
            Err(err) => {
                warn!("Unable to locate a razor: {err}, retrying");
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#in-executables)In executables

Executables should choose a logging implementation and initialize it early in the runtime of the program. Logging implementations will typically include a function to do this. Any log messages generated before the implementation is initialized will be ignored.

The executable itself may use the `log` crate to log as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning)Warning

The logging system may only be initialized once.

[§](https://docs.rs#structured-logging)Structured logging

If you enable the `kv` feature you can associate structured values
with your log records. If we take the example from before, we can include
some additional context besides what’s in the formatted message:

```
use log::{info, warn};
pub fn shave_the_yak(yak: &mut Yak) {
    info!(target: "yak_events", yak:serde; "Commencing yak shaving");
    loop {
        match find_a_razor() {
            Ok(razor) => {
                info!(razor; "Razor located");
                yak.shave(razor);
                break;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                warn!(e:err; "Unable to locate a razor, retrying");
            }
        }
    }
}
```
See the [ kv](https://docs.rs/kv/index.html) module documentation for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-logging-implementations)Available logging implementations

In order to produce log output executables have to use a logger implementation compatible with the facade. There are many available implementations to choose from, here are some of the most popular ones:

- Simple minimal loggers:
- Complex configurable frameworks:
- Adaptors for other facilities:
- For WebAssembly binaries:
- For dynamic libraries:
- You may need to construct an FFI-safe wrapper over `log`to initialize in your libraries

- You may need to construct an FFI-safe wrapper over
- Utilities:

[§](https://docs.rs#implementing-a-logger)Implementing a Logger

Loggers implement the [ Log](https://docs.rs/trait.Log.html) trait. Here’s a very basic example that simply
logs all messages at the

[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Error`[or](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Warn`[levels to stdout:](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Info````
use log::{Record, Level, Metadata};
struct SimpleLogger;
impl log::Log for SimpleLogger {
    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {
        metadata.level() <= Level::Info
    }
    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {
        if self.enabled(record.metadata()) {
            println!("{} - {}", record.level(), record.args());
        }
    }
    fn flush(&self) {}
}
```
Loggers are installed by calling the [ set_logger](https://docs.rs/fn.set_logger.html) function. The maximum
log level also needs to be adjusted via the

[function. The logging facade uses this as an optimization to improve performance of log messages at levels that are disabled. It’s important to set it, as it defaults to](https://docs.rs/fn.set_max_level.html)

`set_max_level`[, so no log messages will ever be captured! In the case of our example logger, we’ll want to set the maximum log level to](https://docs.rs/enum.LevelFilter.html)

`Off`[, since we ignore any](https://docs.rs/enum.LevelFilter.html)

`Info`[or](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Debug`[level log messages. A logging implementation should provide a function that wraps a call to](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Trace`[and](https://docs.rs/fn.set_logger.html)

`set_logger`[, handling initialization of the logger:](https://docs.rs/fn.set_max_level.html)

`set_max_level````
use log::{SetLoggerError, LevelFilter};
static LOGGER: SimpleLogger = SimpleLogger;
pub fn init() -> Result<(), SetLoggerError> {
    log::set_logger(&LOGGER)
        .map(|()| log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Info))
}
```
Implementations that adjust their configurations at runtime should take care to adjust the maximum log level as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#use-with-std)Use with `std`

`set_logger` requires you to provide a `&'static Log`, which can be hard to
obtain if your logger depends on some runtime configuration. The
`set_boxed_logger` function is available with the `std` Cargo feature. It is
identical to `set_logger` except that it takes a `Box<Log>` rather than a
`&'static Log`:

```
pub fn init() -> Result<(), SetLoggerError> {
    log::set_boxed_logger(Box::new(SimpleLogger))
        .map(|()| log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Info))
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#compile-time-filters)Compile time filters

Log levels can be statically disabled at compile time by enabling one of these Cargo features:

- `max_level_off`
- `max_level_error`
- `max_level_warn`
- `max_level_info`
- `max_level_debug`
- `max_level_trace`

Log invocations at disabled levels will be skipped and will not even be present in the
resulting binary. These features control the value of the `STATIC_MAX_LEVEL` constant. The
logging macros check this value before logging a message. By default, no levels are disabled.

It is possible to override this level for release builds only with the following features:

- `release_max_level_off`
- `release_max_level_error`
- `release_max_level_warn`
- `release_max_level_info`
- `release_max_level_debug`
- `release_max_level_trace`

Libraries should avoid using the max level features because they’re global and can’t be changed once they’re set.

For example, a crate can disable trace level logs in debug builds and trace, debug, and info level logs in release builds with the following configuration:

```
[dependencies]
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["max_level_debug", "release_max_level_warn"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-feature-flags)Crate Feature Flags

The following crate feature flags are available in addition to the filters. They are
configured in your `Cargo.toml`.

- `std`allows use of- `std`crate instead of the default- `core`. Enables using- `std::error`and- `set_boxed_logger`functionality.
- `serde`enables support for serialization and deserialization of- `Level`and- `LevelFilter`.

```
[dependencies]
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std", "serde"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#version-compatibility)Version compatibility

The 0.3 and 0.4 versions of the `log` crate are almost entirely compatible. Log messages
made using `log` 0.3 will forward transparently to a logger implementation using `log` 0.4. Log
messages made using `log` 0.4 will forward to a logger implementation using `log` 0.3, but the
module path and file name information associated with the message will unfortunately be lost.

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^2.0.18/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

---
